pemmican.name: Pemmican
pemmican.summary: A calorie-rich mixture of tallow and dried meat, sometimes with berries, invented by Indigenous peoples of North America and later widely used by fur traders and polar explorers.

robert-peary.name: Robert Peary
robert-peary.summary: American Arctic explorer and naval officer credited with reaching the North Pole in 1909, though this is now doubted; proved Greenland an island and studied Inuit survival skills.

fridtjof-nansen.name: Fridtjof Nansen
fridtjof-nansen.summary: A Norwegian explorer, scientist and Nobel Peace laureate who led the first crossing of Greenland in 1888 and reached a record northern latitude in the 1890s.

robert-falcon-scott.name: Robert Falcon Scott
robert-falcon-scott.summary: British naval officer and Antarctic explorer (1868-1912) who led two expeditions and reached the South Pole in January 1912, five weeks after Amundsen, before dying with his men on the return journey.

ernest-shackleton.name: Ernest Shackleton
ernest-shackleton.summary: Anglo-Irish Antarctic explorer (1874–1922) who led three British expeditions during the Heroic Age of Antarctic Exploration, including the famed Endurance expedition.

roald-amundsen.name: Roald Amundsen
roald-amundsen.summary: Norwegian polar explorer (1872-1928) who led the first team to reach the South Pole in 1911, first sailed the Northwest Passage, and reached the North Pole by airship in 1926; he disappeared in 1928 on an Arctic rescue flight.

whale-oil.name: Whale oil
whale-oil.summary: Oil rendered from whale blubber, historically important for lighting and machine lubrication and sometimes called 'train oil', though its use has almost entirely ceased today.

heinrich-klutschak.name: Heinrich Klutschak
heinrich-klutschak.summary: An Austrian-American engineer, artist, naturalist, writer and explorer (1848–1890) who traveled to the Arctic and Southern Atlantic, joining an 1878–1880 expedition searching for the lost Franklin expedition.

caspar-david-friedrich.name: Caspar David Friedrich
caspar-david-friedrich.summary: German Romantic landscape painter (1774–1840) known for symbolic scenes of solitary figures against dramatic skies and ruins, expressing an emotional response to nature.

the-sea-of-ice.name: The Sea of Ice
the-sea-of-ice.summary: 1823–1824 painting by Caspar David Friedrich imagining an Arctic shipwreck half-buried in ice, initially met with incomprehension but now seen as one of his masterpieces.

mitsivarniannga.name: Mitsivarniannga
mitsivarniannga.summary: A Greenlandic shaman (1860-1910) who was among the first to carve tupilait, spirit figures, making a set from driftwood and body parts for a Danish researcher in 1905-1906.

ammassalik-island.name: Ammassalik Island
ammassalik-island.summary: An island in southeastern Greenland's Sermersooq municipality, about 772 square kilometers in area, also known by its Danish name Kong Oscars Ø.

angakkuq.name: Angakkuq
angakkuq.summary: A spiritual and intellectual figure in Inuit culture who serves a role similar to a medicine man or shaman, with comparable figures found among other Alaska Native peoples.

tupilaq.name: Tupilaq
tupilaq.summary: A monster figure in Inuit religion, especially in Greenland, traditionally fashioned by a shaman from animal and human remains to attack an enemy; today carved as a popular art form.

johann-gottlob-von-quandt.name: Johann Gottlob von Quandt
johann-gottlob-von-quandt.summary: German artist, art scholar and collector (1787–1859).

russell-potter.name: Russell Potter
russell-potter.summary: American writer, professor and guitarist whose work covers hip hop culture and 19th-century British Arctic exploration, including his 2007 book Arctic Spectacles.

edward-parry-royal-navy-officer-born-179.name: William Edward Parry
edward-parry-royal-navy-officer-born-179.summary: British Royal Navy officer and explorer (1790–1855) best known for an 1819–1820 expedition through the Parry Channel in search of the Northwest Passage.

northwest-passage.name: Northwest Passage
northwest-passage.summary: A sea route through the Arctic waterways of Canada linking the Atlantic and Pacific, first fully navigated by ship by Roald Amundsen in 1903–1906.

hamburger-kunsthalle.name: Hamburger Kunsthalle
hamburger-kunsthalle.summary: The art museum of Hamburg, Germany, holding one of the country's few collections spanning seven centuries of European art.

th-odore-g-ricault.name: Théodore Géricault
th-odore-g-ricault.summary: French Romantic painter and lithographer (1791 to 1824), best known for his painting The Raft of the Medusa despite his short life.

the-raft-of-the-medusa.name: The Raft of the Medusa
the-raft-of-the-medusa.summary: Over-life-size 1818–1819 oil painting by Théodore Géricault depicting survivors of the 1816 wreck of the French frigate Méduse, an event that became an international scandal.

lady-franklin-bay-expedition.name: Lady Franklin Bay Expedition
lady-franklin-bay-expedition.summary: An 1881 to 1884 US Army expedition to Ellesmere Island in the Canadian Arctic, led by Lieutenant Adolphus Greely to gather scientific data; only six of twenty-five men survived.

united-states-army-signal-corps.name: United States Army Signal Corps
united-states-army-signal-corps.summary: A branch of the U.S. Army handling communication and information systems, also covering military intelligence, weather forecasting and aviation.

adolphus-greely.name: Adolphus Greely
adolphus-greely.summary: American Army officer and polar explorer (1844–1935) who led a disastrous 1881 Arctic expedition and later became the Army's Chief Signal Officer.

ellesmere-island.name: Ellesmere Island
ellesmere-island.summary: Canada's northernmost and third-largest island, part of the Arctic Archipelago, home to the country's most northerly point and only about 144 residents as of 2021.

fort-conger.name: Fort Conger
fort-conger.summary: A former Arctic settlement and research post on Ellesmere Island, Canada, built in 1881 as the base for the first major polar scientific expedition and later used by explorer Robert Peary.

omar-d-conger.name: Omar D. Conger
omar-d-conger.summary: U.S. representative and senator from Michigan (1818–1898) who served in Congress from 1869 to 1881.

british-arctic-expedition.name: British Arctic Expedition
british-arctic-expedition.summary: An 1875–76 British Admiralty mission led by Sir George Nares that tried but failed to reach the North Pole via Smith Sound, while extensively exploring Greenland and Ellesmere Island.

george-nares.name: George Nares
george-nares.summary: George Nares: Royal Navy officer and Arctic explorer (1831–1915) who commanded the Challenger Expedition and led the British Arctic Expedition.

smith-sound.name: Smith Sound
smith-sound.summary: An Arctic sea passage between Greenland and Ellesmere Island, linking Baffin Bay to Kane Basin as part of the Nares Strait.

hms-alert-1856.name: HMS Alert
hms-alert-1856.summary: A 17-gun Royal Navy wooden sloop launched in 1856, noted for Arctic exploration, reaching a record latitude of 82° North in 1876.

hms-discovery-1874.name: HMS Discovery
hms-discovery-1874.summary: A Royal Navy expedition and supply ship purchased in 1874 for the British Arctic Expedition of 1875–1876.

james-clark-ross.name: James Clark Ross
james-clark-ross.summary: A British naval officer and explorer (1800-1862) who led his own Antarctic expedition from 1839 to 1843, confirming the Antarctic continent's existence.

hms-erebus-1826.name: HMS Erebus
hms-erebus-1826.summary: A Royal Navy exploration ship launched in 1826, used in the 1839–1843 Ross expedition to Antarctica and lost in 1848 during Franklin's Arctic expedition.

hms-terror-1813.name: HMS Terror
hms-terror-1813.summary: A Royal Navy bomb vessel built in 1813 that fought in the War of 1812, then became a polar exploration ship, lost with all hands during Sir John Franklin's 1845 Northwest Passage attempt.

ross-ice-shelf.name: Ross Ice Shelf
ross-ice-shelf.summary: Antarctica's largest ice shelf, roughly the size of France, named after Sir James Clark Ross, who discovered it in 1841.

mount-erebus.name: Mount Erebus
mount-erebus.summary: The southernmost active volcano on Earth, on Ross Island in Antarctica, named by explorer James Clark Ross in 1841 after his ship.

winfield-scott-schley.name: Winfield Scott Schley
winfield-scott-schley.summary: American rear admiral (1839–1911) known as the hero of the Battle of Santiago de Cuba during the Spanish–American War.

uss-bear.name: USS Bear
uss-bear.summary: A dual steam- and sail-powered ship built in Scotland in 1874 with thick sides for ice work; as a US revenue cutter she helped rescue the 1884 Lady Franklin Bay Expedition and later served on Antarctic expeditions.

uss-thetis-1881.name: USS Thetis
uss-thetis-1881.summary: A wooden-hulled steam whaler built in 1881 and acquired by the US Navy in 1884 to help relieve the polar expedition led by Lieutenant Adolphus Greely.

albert-hastings-markham.name: Albert Hastings Markham
albert-hastings-markham.summary: British Royal Navy officer, explorer and author who designed the flag of New Zealand and was made a Knight Commander of the Order of the Bath in 1903.

farthest-north.name: Farthest North
farthest-north.summary: The most northerly latitude reached by explorers before the first successful expedition to the North Pole made the record obsolete.

john-franklin.name: John Franklin
john-franklin.summary: British Royal Navy officer and Arctic explorer who led expeditions into the Canadian Arctic; his ships became icebound off King William Island in 1845, and he died there in June 1847, with his entire crew later perishing.

francis-crozier.name: Francis Crozier
francis-crozier.summary: Royal Navy officer and Arctic and Antarctic explorer (1796–1848) who was second-in-command to John Franklin and captain of HMS Terror during Franklin's fatal attempt to find the Northwest Passage.

king-william-island.name: King William Island
king-william-island.summary: A large Arctic island in Canada's Nunavut territory where Franklin's ill-fated 1845 expedition became icebound and where the last known written message from its crew was later found.

hinrich-johannes-rink.name: Hinrich Johannes Rink
hinrich-johannes-rink.summary: A Danish geologist and glaciology pioneer (1819–1893) who spent years in Greenland, became its scholar and administrator, introduced early home rule, and made the first systematic collection of Greenlandic oral tradition.

bal-gangadhar-tilak.name: Bal Gangadhar Tilak
bal-gangadhar-tilak.summary: Indian nationalist (1856-1920) and early advocate of self-rule, known for the slogan 'Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it!'; allied with other independence leaders including Jinnah.

the-arctic-home-in-the-vedas.name: The Arctic Home in the Vedas
the-arctic-home-in-the-vedas.summary: A 1903 book by Bal Gangadhar Tilak arguing, from analysis of Vedic hymns, that the Aryans originally lived near the North Pole before migrating around 8000 BCE due to climate change; now seen as pseudoscientific.
the-arctic-home-in-the-vedas.source_title: The Arctic Home in the Vedas

rasmus-berthelsen.name: Rasmus Berthelsen
rasmus-berthelsen.summary: Greenlandic teacher, poet and artist (1827–1901), considered perhaps the first Greenlandic author of the post-Viking age and known for his hymn-writing.

henning-jakob-henrik-lund.name: Henrik Lund
henning-jakob-henrik-lund.summary: Greenlandic lyricist, painter, and Lutheran pastor (1875 to 1948) who wrote the lyrics to Greenland's national anthem, "Nunarput, utoqqarsuanngoravit."

jonathan-petersen.name: Jonathan Petersen
jonathan-petersen.summary: Greenlandic songwriter (1881–1961) who composed the music for Greenland's national anthem, adopted in 1916, and wrote the words and music of its secondary anthem.

leopold-mcclintock.name: Francis Leopold McClintock
leopold-mcclintock.summary: Irish Royal Navy officer and Arctic explorer (1819-1907) who confirmed the fate of the lost Franklin expedition using Inuit-sourced reports gathered by John Rae, though his claim that Franklin had found the Northwest Passage before his death was false.

thule.name: Thule
thule.summary: A legendary, extremely remote northern land described by ancient Greek and Roman writers, later variously identified with places like Iceland, Greenland or Scandinavia.

james-fitzjames.name: James Fitzjames
james-fitzjames.summary: A British Royal Navy officer and explorer (1813-1848) who captained HMS Erebus on Franklin's lost Arctic expedition, dying near Erebus Bay after the ships were abandoned off King William Island; his remains were identified in 2024.

back-river-nunavut.name: Back River
back-river-nunavut.summary: A roughly 974-kilometre Canadian river flowing through the Northwest Territories and Nunavut to the Arctic Ocean, also historically called Backs River or the Great Fish River.

henry-wadsworth-longfellow.name: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow
henry-wadsworth-longfellow.summary: American poet and educator (1807–1882) known for "Paul Revere's Ride" and The Song of Hiawatha, and the first American to fully translate Dante's Divine Comedy.

yakov-sannikov.name: Yakov Sannikov
yakov-sannikov.summary: Russian explorer active around 1800 who charted several New Siberian Islands and reported a phantom "new land" that became known as Sannikov Land.

matvei-gedenshtrom.name: Matvei Gedenshtrom
matvei-gedenshtrom.summary: A Russian explorer of Northern Siberia, writer and public servant, also known by the Swedish name Mathias Hedenström, who lived from 1780 to 1845.

kotelny-island.name: Kotelny Island
kotelny-island.summary: Arctic island in Russia's New Siberian Islands group, between the Laptev and East Siberian Seas; at 23,165 square kilometres it is among the 50 largest islands in the world.

sannikov-land.name: Sannikov Land
sannikov-land.summary: A phantom island believed to exist in the Arctic Ocean after being reported by explorer Yakov Sannikov in 1811, becoming a 19th-century Russian myth.

salomon-august-andr-e.name: S. A. Andrée
salomon-august-andr-e.summary: A Swedish engineer, physicist and polar explorer (1854-1897) who died leading a failed attempt to reach the North Pole by hydrogen balloon, along with his two companions.

knut-fr-nkel.name: Knut Frænkel
knut-fr-nkel.summary: A Swedish engineer and arctic explorer who died around October 1897 during S. A. Andrée's failed Arctic balloon expedition to reach the North Pole.

nils-strindberg.name: Nils Strindberg
nils-strindberg.summary: Swedish photographer and scientist (1872–1897), one of the three members of S. A. Andrée's ill-fated 1897 Arctic balloon expedition.

svalbard.name: Svalbard
svalbard.summary: A Norwegian Arctic archipelago between mainland Norway and the North Pole, used by whalers from the 17th-18th centuries and later developed for coal mining; recognized as Norwegian territory in 1920.

open-polar-sea.name: Open Polar Sea
open-polar-sea.summary: Once-widely believed but ultimately disproven theory of an ice-free sea encircling the North Pole, which motivated numerous Arctic exploration expeditions.

eduard-von-toll.name: Eduard von Toll
eduard-von-toll.summary: A Russian geologist and Arctic explorer of Baltic German descent who led a 1900-1902 expedition searching for the legendary Sannikov Land and vanished with a small party of explorers near Bennett Island.

laptev-sea.name: Laptev Sea
laptev-sea.summary: A marginal sea of the Arctic Ocean off Siberia, named after Russian explorers Dmitry and Khariton Laptev, with a severe climate and shallow, mostly frozen waters.

bennett-island.name: Bennett Island
bennett-island.summary: The largest of Russia's De Long Islands in the East Siberian Sea, about 150 square kilometres in area and part of Yakutia.

elisha-kent-kane.name: Elisha Kent Kane
elisha-kent-kane.summary: US Navy surgeon and Arctic explorer who served as senior medical officer on an expedition searching for the lost explorer John Franklin, then led a second one, reaching further north than any expedition before him.

isaac-israel-hayes.name: Isaac Israel Hayes
isaac-israel-hayes.summary: American Arctic explorer, physician and politician (1832–1881) who commanded a Civil War hospital and later served in the New York State Assembly; wrote The Open Polar Sea (1867) about his voyage toward the North Pole.

matthew-fontaine-maury.name: Matthew Fontaine Maury
matthew-fontaine-maury.summary: American naval officer and oceanographer (1806–1873), nicknamed the 'Pathfinder of the Seas', whose 1855 book was the first comprehensive study of oceanography.

charles-francis-hall.name: Charles Francis Hall
charles-francis-hall.summary: American Arctic explorer (c.1821–1871) known for collecting Inuit testimony about the 1845 Franklin Expedition and for dying under suspicious circumstances, possibly poisoned, while leading the Polaris North Pole expedition.

polaris-expedition.name: Polaris expedition
polaris-expedition.summary: A U.S.-funded 1871–1873 attempt to reach the North Pole led by Charles Francis Hall, notable for reaching a record 82°29′ N by ship despite troubled leadership.

william-h-seward.name: William H. Seward
william-h-seward.summary: U.S. Secretary of State from 1861 to 1869, and earlier governor of New York and a U.S. senator; an opponent of slavery's spread who negotiated the U.S. purchase of Alaska.

united-states-coast-and-geodetic-survey.name: United States Coast Survey
united-states-coast-and-geodetic-survey.summary: The name, from 1836 to 1878, of the first scientific agency of the U.S. government, responsible for mapping and charting the American coast.
united-states-coast-and-geodetic-survey.source_title: United States Coast and Geodetic Survey

nils-gustaf-ekholm.name: Nils Gustaf Ekholm
nils-gustaf-ekholm.summary: Swedish meteorologist (1848–1923) who led a geophysical expedition to Spitsbergen in 1882–1883.

spitsbergen.name: Spitsbergen
spitsbergen.summary: The largest island of Norway's Svalbard archipelago in the Arctic, used as a whaling base in the 17th and 18th centuries and later for coal mining.

royal-swedish-academy-of-sciences.name: Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences
royal-swedish-academy-of-sciences.summary: An independent Swedish scientific organization founded in 1739 that promotes natural sciences and mathematics and awards the Nobel Prizes in physics and chemistry.

treaty-of-kiel.name: Treaty of Kiel
treaty-of-kiel.summary: A January 1814 treaty in which Denmark's Frederick VI ceded Heligoland to Britain and Norway to Sweden in exchange for Swedish Pomerania, while keeping Greenland, Iceland and the Faroe Islands.

british-arctic-territories.name: British Arctic Territories
british-arctic-territories.summary: British-claimed islands north of mainland Canada, defined in 1880 based on 16th-century discoveries by Martin Frobisher, and transferred to Canada that same year; now known as the Arctic Archipelago.

northwest-territories.name: Northwest Territories
northwest-territories.summary: A territory of northern Canada formed in 1870 on lands of the Dene and Inuvialuit peoples, with Yellowknife as its capital since 1967.

hudson-s-bay-company.name: Hudson's Bay Company
hudson-s-bay-company.summary: A Canadian company founded in 1670 that controlled the North American fur trade and acted as the de facto government of British North America until 1869, later becoming a department store chain before liquidating in 2025.

rupert-s-land.name: Rupert's Land
rupert-s-land.summary: A territory in British North America based on the Hudson Bay drainage basin, granted to the Hudson's Bay Company for trade from 1670 to 1870, covering much of present-day Canada.

jane-franklin.name: Jane Franklin
jane-franklin.summary: British explorer and traveller (1791–1875), second wife of Arctic explorer John Franklin, known for philanthropy in Australia and for sponsoring searches after his disappearance.

franklin-s-lost-expedition.name: Franklin's lost expedition
franklin-s-lost-expedition.summary: A failed 1845 British Arctic voyage led by Sir John Franklin to chart the Northwest Passage; both ships became icebound near King William Island and all 129 men died.

klondike-gold-rush.name: Klondike Gold Rush
klondike-gold-rush.summary: A migration of roughly 100,000 prospectors to Yukon's Klondike region between 1896 and 1898 after gold was discovered there, immortalized in films, literature and photographs.

edward-stanley-15th-earl-of-derby.name: 15th Earl of Derby
edward-stanley-15th-earl-of-derby.summary: British statesman (1826–1893) who served twice as Foreign Secretary, including 1874 to 1878, and twice as Colonial Secretary.

pytheas.name: Pytheas
pytheas.summary: Greek geographer and explorer from Massalia (born c. 350 BC) who sailed to Northern Europe around 325 BC, circumnavigating Britain and becoming the first to describe the Arctic and the midnight sun.

amarok-wolf.name: Amarok
amarok-wolf.summary: A gigantic solitary wolf in Inuit religion said to devour anyone who hunts alone at night; some Arctic peoples use the word more broadly for any wolf.

charles-vallancey.name: Charles Vallancey
charles-vallancey.summary: British army officer and surveyor (1731–1812) who was posted to Ireland and became an authority on Irish antiquities, though some of his theories are now rejected.

william-forbes-skene.name: William Forbes Skene
william-forbes-skene.summary: Scottish lawyer, historian and antiquary (1809–1892) who co-founded the legal firm Skene Edwards.

kintyre.name: Kintyre
kintyre.summary: A peninsula in western Scotland stretching about 30 miles from the Mull of Kintyre to Loch Tarbert, long a prized area for Scots migrating from Ulster and later Viking settlers.

gaius-julius-solinus.name: Solinus
gaius-julius-solinus.summary: Latin grammarian, geographer and compiler who probably flourished in the early to mid 3rd century AD.

knud-rasmussen.name: Knud Rasmussen
knud-rasmussen.summary: A Greenlandic-Danish polar explorer and anthropologist (1879–1933), called the 'father of Eskimology', and the first European to cross the Northwest Passage by dog sled.

north-star-bay.name: North Star Bay
north-star-bay.summary: Bay in northwest Greenland where Knud Rasmussen founded the trading post and mission he named Thule in 1910; it is now home to the U.S. Pituffik Space Base.

chesterfield-inlet-nunavut.name: Chesterfield Inlet
chesterfield-inlet-nunavut.summary: A Hudson Bay hamlet in Nunavut, Canada, known to the Inuit as Igluligaarjuk and considered the territory's oldest community.

franz-boas.name: Franz Boas
franz-boas.summary: German-American anthropologist (1858–1942), called the "Father of American Anthropology," known for opposing scientific racism and mentoring many later influential anthropologists.

sadlermiut.name: Sadlermiut
sadlermiut.summary: An Inuit group that lived in near isolation around Hudson Bay until the early 20th century, once thought to descend from the Dorset culture though genetic studies show sole Inuit ancestry.

dorset-culture.name: Dorset culture
dorset-culture.summary: A Paleo-Eskimo culture in the North American Arctic, lasting from about 500 BCE until it died out by 1000–1500 CE, before the Thule (proto-Inuit) arrived. Inuit legends recall its people as the Tuniit.

john-ross-royal-navy-officer.name: John Ross
john-ross-royal-navy-officer.summary: British naval officer and explorer (1777–1856), uncle of Antarctic explorer James Clark Ross, whom he accompanied on Arctic expeditions.

inughuit.name: Inughuit
inughuit.summary: An ethnic subgroup of Greenlandic Inuit, the northernmost group of Inuit and people in North America, making up about 1% of Greenland's population.
